rtr.text: Oana Vitellius I, a young defender in New Prahv, rants in a bar that she cannot keep up and blames herself for her client's ruin, when Tarem introduces himself and offers her a proposal to transfer the memories and training of her dead grandfather to her.
She remembers recognizing Tarem as Dimir and angrily refusing, vowing to earn the right to destroy him, and the next day, newly driven, she wins five trials and is not late for a single one.

Decades later, when she is an esteemed arbiter, Tarem, unaged, waits in her home and demands that she acquit an unknown accused in an Izzet League theft case as payment, then asks her when she last saw her granddaughter, and Oana realizes she has no grandchildren and that her memory of the offer was altered.

Her true memory restored, she recalls that she had reasoned the transfer was legal and agreed to one favor to be named later, so she resigns, confesses and recuses herself from her cases, seeking a lawyer.
